html:
In 1241 Mongol armies swept into Central Europe, crushing a Polish army at Legnica and a Hungarian one at Mohi within two days of each other. A year later they turned back east.

The campaign was led by Batu Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan, with the great general Subutai. From 1236 they conquered the Volga Bulgars and the Cumans of the steppe and destroyed the principalities of Kievan Rus', sacking Kyiv in 1240. Then they struck west in two arms:

  • In the north they ravaged Poland and beat a Polish and German army at the Battle of Legnica on 9 April 1241.
  • In the south the main army destroyed the army of King Béla IV at the Battle of Mohi on 11 April, and laid waste to Hungary.

In 1242 they withdrew. The Great Khan Ögedei had died, and the princes went home to decide the succession. Batu stayed on the Volga and founded the Golden Horde, which ruled the Rus' for over two centuries. The invasion was part of the wider Mongol conquests.
sum: In 1241 Mongol armies swept into Central Europe, crushing a Polish army at Legnica and a Hungarian one at Mohi within two days of each other. A year later they turned back east.
